summary: Unexpected invoice spike due to byte-level tokenizer fallback in batch-embed job
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a ~12x spike on a single finalized invoice line after a nightly batch-embed job ran on 2026-03-13. NarrativeAI says the job uploads mixed binary/text logs from their ingestion pipeline; they’ve been running the same job for months without similar bills. Suspected root cause: tokenizer produced an unexpectedly large token count for a subset of requests.

Impact:
- NarrativeAI received a $18,200 charge attributed to a single batch job (normal monthly ~ $2.4k).
- Their application degraded to pay-as-you-go hosted pricing for fallback items during the period.
- Business impact: blocker for month-end budget; customer requests provisional credit and technical explanation.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod) in us-west region.
- Batch ingestion pipeline using upload endpoint /v1/batch/embeddings.
- Model: rw-embed-large-v2.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Upload a ~220MB gzip containing mixed text files + occasional binary log blobs via the customer batch API key.
2) Start the batch job with content-type omitted (their CI archive tooling previously relied on inference API to infer encoding).
3) Observe tokenization report in job summary showing per-document token counts: many docs showing token_count > 1,000,000.
4) Invoice finalized the next day.

Logs / evidence attached by customer (snippets redacted):
- batch_job_id: job_20260313_narr_089a
- sample file name: ingestion-20260313-logs-47.gz
- per-request token_count entries: [124, 138, 1_235_482, 1_048_992, 131, 142] (customer scrubbed to show pattern).
- request headers: several requests missing Content-Type and contained non-UTF8 byte sequences.

Customer request:
- Emergency provisional credit to cover excessive surge while Redwood investigates (they asked for hold on autopay).
- Technical explanation and permanent mitigation to prevent similar recharges.
comments: 2026-03-14 09:03 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged receipt. Escalating to platform metering and runtime team. SLA-aware — provisional credit requested pending investigation.

2026-03-14 10:12 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Assigned. Reproducing with customer sample archive. Initial hypothesis: tokenizer fallback is operating in byte-level mode when UTF-8 decode fails, which can expand token counts for binary blobs (byte-level tokenizers split into many single-byte tokens).
2026-03-14 13:47 - Priya Nair (Billing): Placed invoice on provisional hold for $18,200 pending review. Suggested temporary refund/credit hold amount $18k if engineering confirms encoding edge-case.

2026-03-14 18:05 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced locally. When Content-Type header missing and body contains >1% non-decodable bytes, tokenizer falls back to byte-level tokenization. Consequence: binary logs compressed inside gzip were expanded to millions of tokens post-decode attempt.
investigation_notes: Confirmed reproduction with customer sample archive: decoder tried utf-8, raised UnicodeDecodeError, runtime caught exception and invoked byte-level tokenization fallback.
Telemetry: 49 requests in job_20260313_narr_089a triggered fallback. Token distribution shows long tail with per-request token counts between 10k and 1.2M.

Recent change: runtime allowed 'best-effort' decoding to avoid failing entire batch when encoding ambiguous. That change was merged 2026-02-28 (PR 2670) and enabled inbound byte streams to be tokenized instead of rejecting.

Metering pipeline counted tokens after tokenization step (expected). No duplicate postbacks or replays observed in billing logs for this job. The high charge is genuine token accounting, not double-billing.
root_cause_summary: Runtime behavior: when UTF-8 decoding fails for an inbound document and Content-Type not provided, tokenizer falls back to byte-level mode. Binary blobs previously surfaced as a small exception are now tokenized and counted, producing huge token counts and unexpected charges.
resolution:
1) Approved provisional credit for full disputed amount pending final reconciliation. Billing issued a credit memo (CM-2026-0314-089) for $18,200 and put autopay on hold for NarrativeAI until 2026-03-20.
2) Code fix: enforce pre-tokenization validation that rejects documents with >0.5% non-decodable byte sequences when content-type is text/*; return 400 with guidance instead of silently falling back. PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2731.
3) Short-term protection: add per-request metering cap of 50k tokens for batch uploads without explicit content-type; any request exceeding cap is flagged for manual review and capped in invoice calculations.
4) Postmortem and follow-up tests added to Tokenization Runbook.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-15 09:30 - Priya Nair (Billing): Credit CM-2026-0314-089 issued. Customer notified and autopay hold applied.
2026-03-15 11:22 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Runtime fix merged and staging rollout started. Canary in us-west to monitor for false positives.
2026-03-15 14:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed provisional credit received; asked for final confirmation once production fix is live and final invoice adjusted.
follow_up_actions: Add encoding-validation unit tests and integration tests to batch-ingest CI (owner: runtime team).
Update public docs about encoding best practices for batch uploads and example headers/content-type. (owner: docs).
Add billing protection: automatic review for per-request token counts > 100k in a single job (owner: billing).
Schedule postmortem with SRE, Billing, and DX teams to review rollout of PR 2731 (target: 2026-03-22).
